label: M4 × 0.7
common_uses: Carburetor bowls, small electronics housings, throttle body covers
pitch_warning: Standard M4 coarse pitch. Verify against rare M4×0.5 fine threads on precision instruments.
pro_note: Small M4 STI taps snap easily if misaligned—use a tap guide block and cutting fluid.

label: M5 × 0.8
common_uses: Engine sensor mounts, motorcycle engine covers, airbox housings
pitch_warning: Standard M5×0.8 pitch. Older JIS Japanese motorcycles occasionally use M5×0.9—check with a pitch gauge.
pro_note: Both 13/64" fractional and 5.2 mm metric bits fall cleanly within standard STI minor diameter tolerance.

label: M6 × 1.0
common_uses: Aluminum valve covers, water pumps, oil pan perimeter bolts, motorcycle cases
pitch_warning: Most common M6 automotive bolt. Do not confuse with 1/4-20 UNC bolts, which look nearly identical at a glance.
pro_note: In very soft cast aluminum, a 6.3 mm bit yields slightly deeper thread engagement than a 1/4" (6.35 mm) bit.

label: M8 × 1.25
common_uses: Exhaust manifold studs, intake manifolds, alternator brackets, brake caliper pins
pitch_warning: Check pitch carefully! European cars and specialty brackets sometimes use M8×1.0 fine thread.
pro_note: Exhaust manifold stud repairs experience extreme heat cycling—use stainless steel inserts or solid bushings.

label: M8 × 1.0
alt_drill: Letter P (0.323" / 8.2 mm) in steel or 21/64" in aluminum
common_uses: Brake bleeder screws, European automotive brackets, bicycle crank/frame fittings
pitch_warning: CRITICAL PITCH WARNING: Do NOT force a common M8×1.25 bolt into an M8×1.0 fine thread repair.
pro_note: Never use wire inserts on tapered hydraulic sealing seats unless specifically approved by the OEM service manual.

label: M10 × 1.5
common_uses: Domestic/European engine mounts, transmission bellhousings, general machinery
pitch_warning: #1 PITCH MISTAKE: Japanese cars (Honda, Toyota, Subaru, Nissan) and motorcycles usually use M10×1.25 or M10×1.0, NOT M10×1.5!
pro_note: Measure your original bolt with a thread pitch gauge before buying a kit—M10 has three active automotive pitches.

label: M10 × 1.25
common_uses: Japanese automotive engine blocks, brake caliper brackets, motorcycle cylinder/frame mounts
pitch_warning: CRITICAL PITCH WARNING: Hardware-store M10 bolts are usually M10×1.5. Do NOT mix M10×1.25 JIS fine thread with M10×1.5!
pro_note: For safety-critical brake caliper mounting brackets, check OEM service manuals first before attempting any insert repair.

label: M10 × 1.0
common_uses: Small engine spark plugs, banjo brake fittings, O2/pressure sensors, VW/Audi components
pitch_warning: Extra-fine 1.0 mm pitch—verify carefully against M10×1.25 before tapping.
pro_note: If repairing a small spark plug port, consider a solid flanged insert so the plug cannot back the insert out later.

label: M12 × 1.75
common_uses: Subframe mounts, starter motor bolts, GM/Ford metric bellhousings, heavy industrial machinery
pitch_warning: M12 comes in 1.75 (coarse), 1.5 (fine), and 1.25 (extra fine). Always gauge the original fastener first.
pro_note: 31/64" (0.4844") fits inside a standard 1/2" cordless drill chuck without needing a reduced-shank bit.

label: M12 × 1.5
common_uses: Oil drain plugs (Toyota, BMW, Honda motorcycles), suspension bolts, head bolt repair kits
pitch_warning: Common oil drain plug size—confirm whether your pan uses M12×1.5, M12×1.25, or M14×1.5 before drilling!
pro_note: For aluminum oil pans that get unbolted at every oil change, a solid flanged bushing (Time-Sert style) resists backing out much better than a spring coil.
solid_insert_query: M12x1.5 drain plug thread repair kit solid insert

label: M12 × 1.25
common_uses: Modern automotive & motorcycle spark plugs, Nissan/Subaru suspension & oil drain plugs
pitch_warning: Extra-fine 1.25 mm pitch! Never confuse with M12×1.5 drain plugs or M12×1.75 structural bolts.
pro_note: For stripped cylinder head spark plug holes, solid thin-wall inserts are strongly preferred over open wire coils to ensure gas-tight sealing and heat transfer.
solid_insert_query: M12x1.25 spark plug solid thread repair kit

label: M14 × 1.5
alt_drill: 9/16" (0.5625" / 14.29 mm in aluminum) – check your kit manual!
common_uses: Honda/Acura/Ford/Hyundai aluminum oil drain pans, hydraulic fittings, chassis bolts
pitch_warning: Do NOT confuse M14×1.5 oil drain plugs with M14×1.25 spark plugs or M14×2.0 coarse machinery bolts!
pro_note: CHUCK WARNING: A 14.5 mm (0.571") bit will NOT fit a standard 1/2" (13 mm) drill chuck unless it has a 1/2" or 3/8" reduced shank. Solid inserts are best for oil drain pans.
amazon_kit_query: M14x1.5 oil drain plug thread repair kit
solid_insert_query: M14x1.5 solid insert drain plug repair kit

label: M14 × 1.25
alt_drill: Many spark plug kits use a piloted no-drill reamer tap—verify kit instructions!
common_uses: Automotive, lawnmower, chainsaw, and marine cylinder head spark plug ports
pitch_warning: Dedicated 1.25 mm spark plug pitch—never use an M14×1.5 drain plug kit in a cylinder head!
pro_note: Most mechanics prefer a piloted no-drill solid insert system (Sav-A-Thread or Time-Sert style) with heavy grease on the flutes to catch aluminum chips.
amazon_kit_query: M14x1.25 spark plug thread repair kit
solid_insert_query: M14x1.25 solid spark plug insert kit

label: M16 × 2.0
common_uses: Heavy equipment frames, tractor hitches, industrial die plates, heavy suspension mounts
pitch_warning: Verify M16×2.0 coarse vs. M16×1.5 fine pitch common on axles and hydraulic ports.
pro_note: CHUCK WARNING: Requires a 1/2" reduced-shank Silver & Deming drill bit and high-torque low-RPM drill or magnetic drill press.
solid_insert_query: M16x2.0 heavy duty solid thread insert

label: #6-32 UNC
alt_drill: 3.8 mm (0.1496") — avoid 5/32" (0.156") as it cuts threads too shallow!
common_uses: US electrical outlet/junction boxes, avionics panels, firearm optics & small enclosures
pitch_warning: Standard US #6 machine screw. Do not confuse with metric M3.5 or M4 screws.
pro_note: Because 5/32" fractional bits are slightly oversized for #6-32 STI, stick to a #25 wire-gauge bit or 3.8 mm metric bit.

label: #8-32 UNC
common_uses: Light fixtures, ceiling electrical boxes, small engine throttle linkages, tool housings
pitch_warning: Very close in diameter to M4×0.7—test in a known nut checker before drilling.
pro_note: 11/64" is a standard fractional bit found in almost every household drill index.

label: #10-24 UNC
common_uses: Lawnmower & chainsaw housings, appliance frames, aluminum boat accessories
pitch_warning: CRITICAL PITCH WARNING: #10 screws are split almost 50/50 between #10-24 (coarse) and #10-32 (fine)!
pro_note: #10-24 works best in softer castings like aluminum; verify TPI before ordering your insert kit.

label: #10-32 UNF
alt_drill: #7 (0.2010" / 5.1 mm) for tighter fit in steel
common_uses: Server racks, aircraft & marine hardware, carburetor & distributor plates
pitch_warning: Confirm 32 TPI fine thread vs. #10-24 coarse or M5×0.8 metric (which is within 0.2 mm diameter!).
pro_note: If tapping hard steel, a #7 (0.201") bit provides slightly fuller STI threads than 13/64" (0.203").

label: 1/4-20 UNC
common_uses: Camera tripods, American V8 valve covers & oil pans, Harley-Davidson covers, shop jigs
pitch_warning: Most common US bolt size! Still verify it is not 1/4-28 UNF or M6×1.0 metric before drilling.
pro_note: 17/64" is included in standard 29-piece fractional drill indexes—never drill with a 1/4" bit (too small, will snap STI tap).

label: 1/4-28 UNF
common_uses: Grease fittings (Zerk), classic American carburetors, aircraft & racing linkages
pitch_warning: Fine 28 TPI thread—do NOT confuse with standard 1/4-20 UNC or 1/8" NPT tapered pipe threads on grease fittings.
pro_note: All-in-one kits include the exact Letter G or 6.6 mm bit so you don't need to buy a full letter drill set.

label: 5/16-18 UNC
common_uses: Small-block Chevy/Ford intake manifolds, water pumps, thermostat housings,Harley primary covers
pitch_warning: Nearly identical in diameter to M8×1.25 metric! Imported or post-2000 domestic engines often use M8×1.25 instead.
pro_note: Watch out for coolant jackets behind water pump and intake manifold bolt holes—measure blind hole depth before drilling!

label: 3/8-16 UNC
common_uses: V8 exhaust manifolds, alternator/AC brackets, transmission housings, shop vises & machinery
pitch_warning: Verify 16 TPI coarse vs. 3/8-24 UNF fine thread used on fuel/flare and flywheel assemblies.
pro_note: If a previous 3/8-16 wire coil already pulled out, step up to an oversized solid bushing (Big-Sert style) rather than stacking coils.

label: 3/8-24 UNF
alt_drill: Letter W (0.3860" / 9.8 mm) for tighter fit in steel
common_uses: Torque converter lugs, classic brake fittings, marine outboard assemblies
pitch_warning: Fine 24 TPI thread—never force a common 3/8-16 bolt into a 3/8-24 fine hole!
pro_note: Keep tap perfectly square to the mounting boss using a drill guide or tap block.

label: 7/16-14 UNC
common_uses: Cylinder head bolts (classic V8), rocker arm studs, heavy engine block accessories, seat belt anchors
pitch_warning: Rocker studs and head bolts often mix 7/16-14 (block side) with 7/16-20 (nut side)—confirm which end stripped!
pro_note: For cylinder head bolts or safety anchors, always verify OEM repair procedures; deep solid inserts are typically required for high clamp loads.

label: 1/2-13 UNC
common_uses: Tractor housings, truck frame brackets, machine table T-slots, heavy cast-iron bases
pitch_warning: Confirm 13 TPI coarse thread! Older machinery occasionally uses obsolete 1/2-12 BSW British Whitworth—do not mix!
pro_note: CHUCK WARNING: 17/32" (0.531") exceeds a 1/2" drill chuck capacity—buy a 1/2" reduced-shank bit or an all-in-one kit with a stepped shank.

label: 5/8-11 UNC
common_uses: Agricultural implements, excavator & loader castings, heavy hitch & structural plates
pitch_warning: Confirm 11 TPI UNC vs. 5/8-18 UNF fine thread used on heavy tie-rods and hydraulic cylinders.
pro_note: CHUCK WARNING: 21/32" requires a 1/2" reduced-shank drill bit, heavy cutting oil, and slow RPM to avoid work-hardening.
